assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

**Agent.** Claude Code's permission system is tool-agnostic: any tool call that is
not covered by an allow rule opens a blocking modal, and a `PreToolUse` hook
returning `permissionDecision: "ask"` forces that modal for a named tool
regardless of the allowlist (this is exactly the mechanism the sibling cell
`2-19 tool-gate-permission-prompt` already uses for `Bash`). Nothing in the
product distinguishes read-only tools here — `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebSearch`
gate the same way `Write` and `Bash` do. The #1861 live run against 2.1.259
confirmed the agent side directly: with the daemon's hook matcher temporarily
set to `Read`, a modal on `Read` delivered `PermissionRequest tool=Read`. So the
agent raises the dialog and Claude Code even fires the hook event for it — the
loss is entirely on the subscriber side.

**Daemon — this is the defect the row exists to catch.** irrlicht installs
`PermissionRequest` with a nine-alternative TOOL-NAME allowlist:

    hookMatcher = "Bash|Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|WebFetch|mcp__.*|AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode"
    (core/adapters/inbound/agents/claudecode/hookinstaller.go, `hookMatcher`)

Claude Code matches a Notification/PermissionRequest matcher against the tool
name, so a modal on `Read` / `Glob` / `Grep` / `LS` / `WebSearch` / `Task` /
`Skill` / `SlashCommand` delivers NOTHING to the daemon. `PermissionPending` is
never set, so `ClassifyState`'s rule 0 (`permission_prompt` → waiting) never
fires.

**And there is no lower rung that re-derives it.** Walking the ladder in
`core/application/services/state_classifier.go` for an open `Read` with the
prompt on screen:

- `permission_prompt` (hook tier) — not set, per the matcher above.
- `transcript_permission_prompt` — claudecode's parser never sets
  `TranscriptPermissionPending`; that signal is copilot's
  `permission.requested`/`permission.completed` pair (#1256).
- `user_blocking_tool` — `isUserBlockingTool` is exactly
  `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode|question|ask_user_question|exit_plan_mode|ask_user`
  (core/domain/session/metrics.go). `Read` is not in it.
- `open_tool_stalled` (#488, the transcript fallback for a hook that can't
  reach the daemon) — armed only by `HasOpenEditPermissionTool`, and
  `isPermissionGatedEditTool` matches exactly
  `edit|write|multiedit|notebookedit|write_file` (metrics.go). `Read` is not in
  it, so the fallback is never even armed.
- `idle_prompt` / `session_error` / `agent_done` — a turn with an open tool call
  is not done.
- default `transcript_activity` → **working**.

So on `main` the session reads `working` for the entire time the user is looking
at a `Read` permission modal, and the recording will show ONE waiting episode
(the `Write` half) where the scenario requires two. The gap is not an inference:
`core/domain/session/signal_hold.go` states it in the source, in
`permissionPromptHoldTimeout`'s doc comment, which enumerates the same matcher
and splits it into "COVERED (expiry is soft): Write, Edit, MultiEdit,
NotebookEdit" vs "NOT COVERED (expiry is silent): Bash, WebFetch, mcp__.*,
AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode" — a coverage table written for the tools that ARE
in the matcher, which by construction says nothing at all about the ones that
are not.

`daemon=bug`, not `incapable`: the trace exists and reaches Claude Code's hook
layer; only irrlicht's installed matcher throws it away. **PR #1867 (open, not
merged; this worktree is based on `main` without it) widens `hookMatcher` to
`"*"`, which is the fix.** The spec below therefore asserts the CORRECT arc
(two distinct waiting episodes) and is flagged `known_failing`.

**Driver.** `replaydata/agents/claudecode/driver-interactive.sh` implements
`send`, `keys`, `wait_turn` and `sleep` (verified with
`driver_step_types_from_file`), which is every step the recipe needs.
caveats: PR #1867 is the open fix (hookMatcher widened to "*"). It is NOT merged and this worktree is based on main without it, so this cell is assessed against main and records known_failing. When #1867 lands, re-record and drop known_failing — nothing else in the cell should need to change.

VACUOUS-PASS CONDITION: this cell passes while proving nothing if the READ-ONLY modal never actually opens. A session in which Read is pre-approved produces exactly one waiting episode — which is byte-for-byte what the bug also produces, so the recording cannot tell 'the daemon missed the second gate' from 'there was no second gate'. Two guards, both load-bearing: (1) the recipe's own PreToolUse ask hook appends a line to .gate-hook.log BEFORE emitting its ask decision, so record can assert the gate fired twice rather than inferring it from an absence; (2) the recipe pins permissions.defaultMode=default with an empty allow list.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTIES, to be re-probed at record time, not trusted: the session must NOT run under auto mode, plan mode, --dangerously-skip-permissions, or acceptEdits, and ~/.claude/settings.json must not carry a user-level permissions.allow entry for Read or Write. Any of these pre-approves one or both halves and silently degrades the cell into a duplicate of 2-19 with a green spec.

The two gates must land as two SEPARATE modals. Claude Code batches independent tool calls into one assistant message; the prompt creates a real data dependency (read back what step 1 wrote) and says so explicitly, which is what serialises them. If a recording shows one merged waiting episode, the scenario is explicit that this does NOT satisfy the row — record should re-drive as two turns (Write in turn 1, Read in turn 2) and note the extra ready in the middle of the arc.

The mutating half is deliberately Write rather than the Bash that 2-19 already uses, so the two cells exercise different covered tools; Write is additionally covered by the #488 open_tool_stalled fallback at 30s, so record should answer the first dialog well inside that window or the fallback, not the hook, becomes the thing under test.

sources.note: hookMatcher = "Bash|Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|WebFetch|mcp__.*|AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode" — the nine-alternative tool-name allowlist PermissionRequest is installed with. Read/Glob/Grep/LS/WebSearch/Task/Skill/SlashCommand are absent, so their modals deliver no hook.

The full ladder. With PermissionPending unset and Read open, no rung claims the decision until the total default transcript_activity → working. Rule 0 (permission_prompt) is the only rung that would have produced waiting.

isUserBlockingTool (AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode/question/ask_user_question/exit_plan_mode/ask_user) and isPermissionGatedEditTool (edit/write/multiedit/notebookedit/write_file) — the two lower-tier tool-name sets. Read is in neither, so neither user_blocking_tool nor open_tool_stalled can re-derive the prompt.

permissionPromptHoldTimeout's doc comment enumerates the same nine-alternative matcher and splits it into COVERED (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, re-derivable by SignalOpenToolStalled) vs NOT COVERED. The table is written only for tools inside the matcher — tools outside it never reach a hold at all.
Sibling cell; source of the PreToolUse permissionDecision=ask technique this recipe reuses to force a modal deterministically for a named tool.
driver_step_types_from_file reports send/keys/wait_turn/sleep among its step types — every primitive this recipe needs. driver=ready.

The report. Live run against claude 2.1.259: with the shipped nine-tool matcher a modal on Read delivered 0 hook events; with the matcher set to Read the same modal delivered PermissionRequest tool=Read. A class-1 (tool-named) dialog reached waiting in 0.0 s.
The open, unmerged fix — widens hookMatcher to "*". Not present in this worktree, which is why the cell is known_failing rather than record.

preconditions: claude CLI on PATH and authenticated; version >= 2.1.122 (the daemon's hook-install floor). Assessed against 2.1.259.
irrlichd is recording (--attach against a daemon started with --record, or isolated mode), with the claudecode hook installer already run so PermissionRequest/PostToolUse route to the daemon.

RE-PROBE AT RECORD TIME: the session must not run under auto mode, plan mode, acceptEdits, or --dangerously-skip-permissions, and ~/.claude/settings.json must carry no permissions.allow entry matching Read or Write. Any of these pre-approves a half and hollows the cell out.
no other claudecode session uses the same UUID
setup: Generate a fresh lowercased session UUID
Create an empty cwd under <staging>/cwd/ (claude prompts for trust on first encounter — the driver auto-accepts)

Write the recipe's settings blob as the project-local .claude/settings.json in that cwd: it pins permissions.defaultMode=default with an empty allow list, and installs a PreToolUse hook matching Write|Read that appends one line to .gate-hook.log and then returns permissionDecision=ask. The log line is the cell's own proof-of-gate — see the vacuous-pass caveat.
Confirm .gate-hook.log does not already exist in the cwd before the run.

script.text:
Do exactly these two steps, one at a time. Wait for each step to finish completely before starting the next one; do NOT issue them as parallel tool calls, and do not use any tool other than the two named here.
Step 1: use the Write tool to create a file named gate.txt in the current directory whose entire contents are the single line GATE-OK
Step 2: use the Read tool to read gate.txt back.
When both steps are done, reply with exactly one line containing only the text you read in step 2.

verify: PROOF OF GATE (must fail loudly, never read a missing file as 'no gate'): <cwd>/.gate-hook.log EXISTS and contains at least 2 lines. If the file is absent or short, the run is INCONCLUSIVE — the ask hook never fired, so neither modal opened and nothing below is evidence of anything.

transcript.jsonl contains an assistant tool_use with name=Write and, LATER, a separate assistant tool_use with name=Read, in two different assistant messages (not one batched message) — this is what makes the two episodes distinguishable at all.
the tool_result for the Read tool_use is timestamped AFTER the driver's second keys step, proving the Read call was actually held by a modal rather than executed straight through.
the final assistant message contains the literal token GATE-OK, proving the Read call really executed after approval.
events.jsonl contains a presession_created for proc-<PID> within 1000 ms and a transcript_new for the UUID session within 500 ms of the send.

ASSERTION UNDER TEST (expected to FAIL on main, #1861): events.jsonl shows TWO distinct state_transition→waiting for the UUID with a state_transition→working between them — one bound to the Write gate, one to the Read gate.
events.jsonl shows the session back at ready after the second approval, and STILL ready across the >=10 s trailing idle (no state_transition to waiting in that window).
